text:
sarah.nguyen: Hey team — hitting intermittent `invalid JSON` errors from our ingest when using JSON mode streaming. Seen in staging and one prod request. Logs show a partial object and some non-printable bytes at the start of the first chunk. Example error: 

  consumer error: json: invalid character '\xEF' looking for beginning of value

Attached raw capture (first ~120 bytes):
  EF BB BF 7B 22 63 68 6F 69 63 65 73 22 3A 20 5B 7B 22 74 65 78 74 22 3A 20 22 48 65 6C 6C 6F 22 2C 20 7D 5D 7D 2C 0D 0A
  which decodes to: 
  \uFEFF{"choices": [{"text": "Hello", },]}

This ends up breaking our Go consumer (encoding/json) and also the TS client that concatenates frames. Repro Steps:
  1) python sdk 0.9.1 call stream(..., mode="json") to our server socket
  2) server forwards raw chunks to internal pipeline (Go) which reads stream and json.Decoder.Decode() on each frame
  3) intermittent failures: 'invalid character' or 'unexpected end of JSON input'

mike.chen: Can you paste the exact client call + SDK versions + whether the stream uses CRLF or LF? Also a minimal raw chunk capture (hex or base64) is super helpful.

sarah.nguyen: Sure — python sdk 0.9.1, ts-sdk 1.2.0 in frontend, go consumer is go1.20 using encoding/json. The stream uses CRLF (server uses "\r\n" delimiters). Minimal python send code: 

  ```python
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
  with c.stream(model="redwood-1", mode="json") as s:
      s.send({"prompt": "hi"})
  ```

  Raw capture (hex, first two chunks):
  Chunk A: EF BB BF 7B 22 63 68 6F 69 63 65 73 22 3A 20 5B 7B 22 74 65 78 74 22 3A 20 22 48 22 2C 20 7D 5D 7D 2C 0D 0A
  Chunk B: 7B 22 63 68 6F 69 63 65 73 22 3A 20 5B 7B 22 74 65 78 74 22 3A 20 22 57 6F 72 6C 64 22 7D 5D 7D 2C 0A

  You can see Chunk A starts with EF BB BF (BOM) and has a trailing comma before CRLF. Not every request has BOM, which is why failures are intermittent.

raj.sdk: Thanks — quick suspicion: python serializer was switched to `utf-8-sig` in a prior commit to handle older windows clients; that writes a BOM at the start of the first byte sequence. The BOM will show up in chunk A and break Go's decoder which expects either whitespace or '{'. We'll triage. Can you confirm whether you call `.encode('utf-8-sig')` anywhere or use a wrapper that does?

sarah.nguyen: We don't explicitly call `utf-8-sig`. We're using the pydantic -> json.dumps path, then SDK's internal chunker. I can try a quick test to force plain `utf-8` encode if you want.

alejandro.g: Also note trailing commas in Chunk A — that will create invalid JSON when frames are concatenated or parsed independently. Two separate issues likely: 1) BOM insertion on first chunk, 2) serializer producing trailing commas for single-element objects in some code paths (we saw this in a different serializer revision). Workarounds: strip BOM at reader, or patch serializer to avoid utf-8-sig and remove trailing commas.

dev-bot: Created issue RED-3456: "jsonmode streaming: BOM + trailing-comma causes intermittent parse failures (py/ts/go)" and assigned to eng-ml + sdk team.

mike.chen: Quick mitigation we can push: (a) python SDK hotfix to ensure `.encode('utf-8')` (no BOM) on outgoing chunks, (b) add TrimPrefix logic on Go consumer to remove unicode BOM (UTF8 BOM bytes) before decoding, (c) reject trailing commas in serializer. I'll open a tiny patch for python SDK and a runtime patch for streaming router to normalize CRLF -> LF and strip BOMs.

raj.sdk: Patch ready in branch `fix/jsonmode-bom-3456` — changes: `json_bytes = json_str.encode('utf-8')` not `utf-8-sig`; ensure `json.dumps(..., separators=(",", ":"))` to avoid extra spaces/trailing commas; add tests for CRLF vs LF chunking.

cleo.support: Can you confirm whether this appears on Dedicated/private customers or only hosted? We need to scope incident notifications.

sarah.nguyen: Saw in hosted staging and once in a customer dedicated environment. After switching to test build from `fix/jsonmode-bom-3456` and restarting the staging client, I retried 50 streams and saw zero failures vs ~3/50 before. Good sign.

alejandro.g: Runtime patch also merged: router now normalizes incoming stream frames, trims BOM on first chunk, and collapses CRLF to LF before forwarding. We added a small fuzz test that concatenates partial frames and validates `json.Valid` on each reconstructed message.

mike.chen: Releasing python SDK 0.9.2 with hotfix now. Recommend customers upgrade. For immediate mitigation: set env var `RW_JSONMODE_STRICT=0` on consumers to enable BOM-tolerant parsing, or add pre-read step like: `data = bytes.TrimPrefix(data, []byte{0xEF,0xBB,0xBF})` in Go.

sarah.nguyen: Verified staging after upgrade to py sdk 0.9.2 + runtime patch. No repro in 200 runs. Will schedule rollout to prod next hour. Thanks all.

cleo.support: I'll notify the affected customer and link release notes. Closing once prod is green. :thumbsup:

mike.chen: Closing RED-3456 after verification steps pass. Follow-up: add a note in docs about consistent encoding expectations for JSON mode streaming.

sarah.nguyen: Thanks everyone — saved our ingestion pipeline.
